entities.summary: A full circuit of Harilaid's mobile dunes and exposed Baltic shore, with a safe shore-side view of the offshore Kiipsaare lighthouse.
entities.description: The current RMK route makes a marked circuit around the Harilaid peninsula through gravel track, loose sand and shingle. The landscape is low but physically deceptive: wind, soft footing and the remote 12 km distance matter more than elevation. The coastline and lighthouse setting change, so follow current red pickets and on-site directions rather than treating any downloaded line as navigation-grade.
entities.whyWorthwhile: Harilaid combines a genuinely dynamic coast, broad storm-scale sea atmosphere and one of Estonia's most memorable lighthouse landscapes in a coherent half-day walk.

values.accessPointNote: Drive only to the signed Harilaid rest-area parking. Public transport does not reach the trailhead: RMK uses Kõruse bus stop only as a driving junction. Current RMK information lists space for 20 cars or 5 buses; there are no shops on the peninsula.
values.bestSeason: Official visitor guidance promotes both summer and winter use; choose benign weather and good visibility, especially outside summer.
values.crowding: Usually low away from peak summer periods.
values.exposure: Low fall exposure; high exposure to Baltic wind and rapidly changing coastal weather.
values.recommendedVariant: The full marked peninsula circuit via the safe shore viewpoint for Kiipsaare lighthouse.
specialHazards: current habitat-restoration work: follow posted work-zone directions
private unstable lighthouse: do not approach through the sea or climb
values.technicality: Technically easy walking, made more tiring by 12 km of wind-exposed loose sand and shingle.
values.trailheadCoordinatePrecision: RMK published parking coordinate; OSM route begins about 20 m away on the mapped track.

legacy-access-point.note: Drive only to the signed Harilaid rest-area parking. Public transport does not reach the trailhead: RMK uses Kõruse bus stop only as a driving junction. Current RMK information lists space for 20 cars or 5 buses; there are no shops on the peninsula.

variants.name: Harilaiu full peninsula loop via Kiipsaare
variants.description: The full RMK peninsula circuit: out from the Harilaid parking, north on the inland marked track, a short out-and-back to the safe shore-side lighthouse viewpoint, then south along the mapped western coastal path before returning on the parking spur.

trailhead.name: Harilaid rest-area parking
trailhead.note: The mapped route begins on the parking track, about 20 m from RMK's published parking coordinate.

variants.accessNotes: Use the signed road only as far as the Harilaid rest-area parking. Public transport does not reach the trailhead: RMK uses Kõruse bus stop only as a driving junction. Motor vehicles are prohibited past that parking except for the protected-area exceptions stated by the national park. RMK lists an information board, dry toilet and current capacity for 20 cars or 5 buses; the peninsula has no shops.
variants.seasonalLimitations: Official visitor guidance promotes both summer and winter use, and the current RMK route page announces no closure. Storms, strong wind, ice and snow can materially change difficulty. The shore moves; current red pickets, habitat-work directions, signs and closures supersede the captured line.
variants.waterAvailability: No potable-water source is documented on the route and there are no shops on the peninsula; carry the day's water.
suitabilityConstraints: The route is flat but 12 km of loose sand, shingle and wind exposure can be tiring.
Not suitable for visitors who require a firm, step-free surface.
Do not wade to, enter or climb Kiipsaare lighthouse.
warnings: Kiipsaare lighthouse is private property in the sea on unstable ground; view it from shore and do not climb it.
The shoreline changes. This OSM-derived centerline follows the currently mapped RMK loop but is descriptive, not navigation-grade.
RMK currently flags natterjack-toad habitat-restoration work on Harilaid. It does not announce a route closure, but follow work-zone signs and staff directions.
Do not drive beyond the Harilaid rest-area parking.
Check current RMK and national-park notices plus coastal weather before setting out.
